causalCorrections.implementation: serialize generation-seal and initial-ledger bootstrap across threads and processes with a persistent control/bootstrap-v1.lock byte lock. On Windows open a+b, ensure byte zero exists, seek zero and use msvcrt.locking LK_NBLCK for exactly one byte; on POSIX use fcntl.flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB. Bound contention by busy_timeout_ms using time.monotonic with 10 ms waits; timeout maps to NEWS_GRASP_ENTRY_LEDGER_BUSY. Within the acquired lock re-check generation seal and ledger existence, initialize at most once, then always unlock and close without deleting the lock file. This lock protects bootstrap only; BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus the SQLite slot row remains the sole run ownership authority.
causalCorrections.forbidden: no process-local-only threading lock, no replace retry loop, no lock-file deletion ownership protocol

causalCorrections.implementation: in _connect, keep the new sqlite connection in a nullable local and close it before re-raising any sqlite.Error from row_factory or PRAGMA setup. This specifically releases the Windows sqlite/shm handles when PRAGMA journal_mode discovers a corrupt header before _connect returns.
causalCorrections.forbidden: no gc.collect, sleep retry, copy fallback, delete, or sharing-violation suppression

causalCorrections.implementation: after a healthy verify, parse and hash-validate an existing recovery journal. If it is COMMITTED, return the same eight CONTROL_LEDGER_RECOVERY_V1 keys with status RECOVERY_NOT_REQUIRED, oldGeneration/newGeneration/recoveryId/quarantinePath from that journal, resumed true and externalEffectCount zero, with no filesystem mutation. A healthy ledger with no completed journal continues to raise CleanroomEntryError reason NEWS_GRASP_ENTRY_RECOVERY_NOT_REQUIRED. A corrupt or non-COMMITTED journal follows the existing typed recovery rules. After creating a recovered SQLite generation, execute a FULL WAL checkpoint, close it, reopen through verify, then persist LEDGER_CREATED as V3 requires.
causalCorrections.forbidden: no new public API, schema key, reason, generation increment or journal deletion
